# Privacy and security

This page explains what DrakeFlake changes on your system, what runs as root
and how the root helper limits itself, which links it opens and what it sends
over the network.

## What the app changes

The app edits nothing in your configuration except its own generated files,
plus the two setup steps listed below. Generated files are `.nix` files inside
your flake that start with this line:

```text
# GENERATED by DrakeFlake - safe to delete.
```

Only files with that line, or empty files, are ever overwritten or removed.
Besides those, the app writes:

- `flake.lock`, when you update inputs
- its own settings, logs, backups and caches in your home folder (see
  [Where things are](troubleshooting.md#where-things-are))

## What runs as your user

Almost everything runs as you, without extra rights:

- evaluating your configuration, searching options and packages
- building the system (`nh os build` or `nixos-rebuild build`) when the
  privileged helper activates it afterwards (see below)
- updating flake inputs (`nix flake update`). This deliberately never runs as
  root, so root never fetches the inputs your flake names into the store.
- checking for updates, building images, **Try it**
- writing the generated files when you may write to the flake folder
- the two setup changes when you may write to the file or folder, and locking
  a new flake (`nix flake lock`)

## What runs as root

For the few steps that need root, the app uses a small helper,
`drakeflake-helper`. It starts the helper with the way of getting root it found
(see [pkexec, run0, sudo and the macOS dialog](#pkexec-run0-sudo-and-the-macos-dialog)).
The app finds the helper in the package's `libexec` folder, or at the path in
`DRAKEFLAKE_HELPER` (see
[For packagers and developers](settings.md#for-packagers-and-developers)).

The helper can do exactly four things. Each has its own polkit action, so with
`pkexec` the password prompt tells you what is about to happen. With `run0` or
`sudo` the prompt is that program's own. On a Mac the administrator dialog
names the command.

| Prompt                                                                                                                    | What the helper does                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Password remembered?   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| "Save system settings": "Authentication is required to save the generated NixOS settings files"                           | Writes or removes generated `.nix` files in a flake you may not write to yourself, for example a root-owned `/etc/nixos`.                                                                                                     | No, it asks every time |
| "Activate a NixOS configuration": "Authentication is required to activate this NixOS configuration: …" (with the command) | Activates a system that was already built, by running that system's own `switch-to-configuration` (for switch and boot it also becomes the default boot entry).                                                               | No, it asks every time |
| "Save updated flake inputs": "Authentication is required to save the updated flake.lock"                                  | Replaces `flake.lock` with the new lock file your update produced.                                                                                                                                                            | No, it asks every time |
| "List what a reboot removes": "Authentication is required to list the files a reboot removes from the root file system"   | Lists the names and sizes of what a reboot removes from `/` for the [Impermanence](impermanence.md) page. With a btrfs snapshot name it mounts the file system's top level read-only in a private mount namespace to compare. | Yes, for a short time  |

> **Note:** Saving settings, saving a lock file and activating all change files
> that decide what runs as root, so their prompts never reuse a remembered
> password. Activating also shows the command, so you confirm every activation.

### What the helper checks

The helper checks what it is asked to do before doing anything:

- Writing files: the helper only writes `.nix` files given as absolute paths
  without `..`, inside a flake (never in the Nix store), that are not
  symlinks. A file cannot be both written and removed. It only replaces or
  removes files that are empty or carry the generated header. The new content
  must be a generated module with valid Nix syntax.
- Listing what a reboot removes: the helper only reads names and sizes, never
  file contents. A snapshot name may only hold plain folder names (no `..`, no
  symlinks out of the file system), and the top level is mounted read-only.
- Activating: the helper only activates systems in the Nix store that are
  complete NixOS systems.
- Installing a lock file: the helper only installs a lock file that has the
  shape of a flake lock file, into a local folder that contains a `flake.nix`.
  It reads the new lock file only when it belongs to the user who asked, and
  refuses when it cannot tell who that is.

The helper writes all files of a plan to temporary names first and swaps them
in only when every one was written, with the main generated file last. If a
swap fails, the files already swapped are put back. The app applies the same
rules, plus this order, when it writes the generated files itself.

The polkit actions are only known to polkit when the package is installed
system-wide (see [Installation](installation.md#install-it-system-wide)).

### Tasks run by nh or as root directly

Some tasks are run by nh. The app passes nh the way of getting root it found,
as `--elevation-strategy`:

- **Review and apply…** on the Changes page (this needs nh)
- **Switch to** on the Generations page (NixOS)
- **Cleanup**

A nix-darwin switch is the exception: the app builds as you and then sets
the system profile and activates it under one administrator dialog, so nh
never gets `--elevation-strategy` there.

Without nh, **Cleanup** runs `nix-collect-garbage` as root, and **Switch to**
goes through the helper like **Test** and **Boot**.

Applying uses the helper only for a NixOS host, and only when the helper is
installed and a way of getting root was found. The system is then built as
you and only activated as root. Otherwise applying runs nh or the rebuild
tool:

- With nh, a NixOS host runs `nh os <mode>`. The app first checks whether the
  installed nh knows `--elevation-strategy`. If it does, nh gets the same way
  of getting root. If not, nh asks for root itself, and you answer its
  password prompt in the Console.
- A nix-darwin host with nh builds as you with `nh darwin build`. Then one
  administrator dialog runs a script that points the system profile at the
  new system and activates it.
- Without nh, a NixOS host runs `nixos-rebuild` as root, and a nix-darwin
  host runs `darwin-rebuild switch` as root, so the build runs as root too.

A nix-darwin generation is switched with `darwin-rebuild --switch-generation`
as root.

### pkexec, run0, sudo and the macOS dialog

The app looks for a way to get root in this order:

1. On macOS, the system's administrator dialog (`drakeflake-elevate`, which
   runs the command through `osascript … with administrator privileges`). It
   names the command it is about to run. Setting the system profile and
   activating it share one dialog.
2. A setuid `pkexec` (on NixOS, `/run/wrappers/bin/pkexec`): your desktop's
   polkit password dialog.
3. `run0` (systemd): also polkit, without a setuid program.
4. A setuid `sudo`, only for commands that run in the Console.

When `run0` or `sudo` is used for a command in the Console, the Console says
so. If `run0` or `sudo` asks for your password there, answer in the password
bar above the output (see [Password prompts](applying.md#password-prompts)).
The password goes to that program only and is never shown or logged.

## Links

Links in option descriptions, package metadata and flake inputs come from many
sources. The app only opens links that start with `http://` or `https://`.
Other links (for example `file://`) are not opened. Images in option
descriptions are shown as their text, so viewing documentation does not load
anything from the internet.

## Network access

The app sends nothing about you or your system anywhere. It only uses the
network for:

- fetching your flake inputs and packages, done by Nix itself (evaluating,
  building, updating, **Try it**, images)
- checking flake inputs for updates (`git ls-remote` and HTTP header requests to
  the sources named in your `flake.lock`), by the app and by the tray
- downloading the nix-index command database from GitHub, only when you click
  **Download** on the Packages page
- opening links in your browser when you click them
